newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close weaker in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close weaker in heavy volume.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed weaker on Monday after a volatile day which saw the Hang Seng Index hitting a new record high before retreating on profit-taking and nervousness over China-related red chips , brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed down 133.13 points, or 0.88 percent, at 15,021.23. Turnover was HK$26.33 billion, marginally down on Friday's record figure of HK$26.6 billion.
Earlier in the day, the Hang Seng Index touched a fresh all-time high, rising 167 points to 15,322, as investors showed their bullishness on the territory's July 1 handover to China.
"(It's) very volatile, and very confused," said James Osborne, sales director at ING Barings.
The day was characterised by massive volatility and capital flows, but one broker predicted further short-term record highs because "that's what everybody wants".
A broker with a European institution said much of the liquidity was flowing in from China ahead of the handover, but added the flows were short-term.
